_comment: AUTHORED POLICY DATA — not a generated artifact.
Nothing in scripts/ writes this file. It records decisions a human made, and it is
the input that makes those decisions enforceable: validate_policy.py and
fetch_github_metadata.py both read it. Do not regenerate it, do not prune it to make
a build pass, and do not add an entry without recording who decided and when.
The reasoning behind each entry lives in
form of the same decision, so that the policy fails a build instead of depending on

content_patterns.reason: Identifiers of the known leaked-prompt collections — repository names and the filename stems they publish. Matching an identifier rather than the English phrase is deliberate: the separator is required, so `system_prompts_leaks` and `CL4R1T4S` match while ordinary prose about "leaked system prompts" does not. A pattern that fired on the phrase would flag the exclusion policy's own summary wherever it is indexed, and a check that objects to the document forbidding the thing gets switched off.

star_count_note: observed_stars values are snapshots recorded on observed_on, not durable facts. They are stored deliberately: the point is to make the tradeoff explicit, so that a future reader who notices these are among the most-starred repositories in their category can see the omission was a decision made with full knowledge of their popularity, not an oversight.
